goal.summary: Replace the current conflated skill/event progress model with distinct task progress, skill-invocation progress, retry-attempt telemetry, and aggregate orchestrator progress.
deliverables: Deterministic task graph with skill invocations and attempts
UI surfaces for aggregate, task, skill, attempt, and telemetry state
constraints: Keep this a browser-only deterministic educational simulation
Do not add backend persistence, external services, real model calls, or dependencies
Keep catalog skill definitions separate from executed invocations
Preserve the existing five-stage harness visualization and local reset flow
exclusions: Durable retries or real idempotency storage
Using catalog skills as aggregate denominator items
Summing task, skill, stage, attempt, and event values together

acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Source inspection and deterministic run transcript show lineage and separate record collections.

acceptanceCriteria.outcome: Task progress, skill-invocation progress, and orchestrator aggregate progress are separate values with explicit state and denominator semantics.
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: UI and state inspection show no shared scalar or additive cross-layer calculation.

acceptanceCriteria.outcome: Orchestrator progress aggregates each eligible logical task leaf exactly once using equal weights, while parallel branches and inactive catalog skills are not double-counted.
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Fixture transcript verifies the documented formula and branch identity.

acceptanceCriteria.outcome: Retries create new attempts without extra logical completion credit; telemetry/event counts remain independent from completion; failed, blocked, skipped, cancelled, and indeterminate states remain distinguishable.
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Controlled deterministic retry/failure fixture and visible state metrics.

acceptanceCriteria.outcome: The progress hierarchy is understandable and accessible on desktop and mobile and existing simulator behavior remains intact.

assumptionsAndDecisions.statement: A catalog skill definition is not an executed work item; each invocation gets its own progress identity.
assumptionsAndDecisions.rationale: The research finding separates static capability metadata from run-scoped invocation records.

assumptionsAndDecisions.statement: The first aggregate implementation uses equal weights over eligible logical task leaves.
assumptionsAndDecisions.rationale: It is auditable and avoids inventing effort estimates; weighted units can be added only when defined later.

assumptionsAndDecisions.statement: Orchestrator completion and successful outcome are separate projections.
assumptionsAndDecisions.rationale: A failed or blocked node must not become successful merely because work was resolved.

assumptionsAndDecisions.statement: Retries are deterministic fixtures represented as attempts under one logical invocation; they do not increase aggregate completion credit.
assumptionsAndDecisions.rationale: The local app has no durable retry runtime, so the UI demonstrates the invariant without claiming production durability.

assumptionsAndDecisions.statement: The five existing harness stages remain stage progress and are not included in task aggregate arithmetic.
assumptionsAndDecisions.rationale: Preserves the current harness visualization and avoids double counting nested dimensions.

design.types: ProgressState = not_started | ready | running | succeeded | failed | blocked | skipped | cancelled | indeterminate. TaskNode has taskId, parentTaskId, label, eligible, weight, state, completion. SkillInvocation has invocationId, taskId, skillId, state, completion. Attempt has attemptId, invocationId, attemptNumber, state, checkpoint. TelemetryEvent has eventId, logicalId, kind, sequence, message. OrchestrationRun has orchestrationId, executionId, taskIds, invocationIds, attemptIds, eventIds.
design.identity: Catalog skills remain static by skill.id. Each run creates unique task/invocation/attempt/event IDs. A repeated invocation of the same skill is a distinct invocation record.
design.aggregation: Derive orchestrator completion from eligible logical task leaves only: sum(weight * known completion) / sum(weight). Equal weights are the initial fixture. Keep successProgress, failureCount, blockedCount, skippedCount, and eventsObserved separate. If no eligible known nodes exist, aggregate is indeterminate.
design.flow: Run start materializes a deterministic task graph and invocation records. Stage transitions update the active task/invocation state and append telemetry. Retry creates an attempt record while preserving logical task/invocation identity. The aggregate selector derives from current task records, never from event count or nested skill bars.
design.ui: Add an orchestrator summary as the primary surface, task tree/detail as the work breakdown, active skill invocation detail, attempt history, and a separate telemetry count/trace. Keep catalog cards as capability overview with invocation status only; keep the existing five-stage strip as stage progress.
design.boundaries: All records are in-memory React state for this educational simulator. No persistence, external side effect, real retry, cancellation guarantee, or server API is introduced.

risks: Parent and child records may be double-counted.
Skill catalog definitions may be mistaken for executed work.
Event count may be mistaken for progress.
Dense hierarchy may be inaccessible or overflow on mobile.
mitigations: Aggregate only unique eligible logical task leaves and test parent/child fixtures.
Use invocation IDs separate from skill IDs.
Keep attempts under invocation identity and calculate from logical node state.
Use semantic lists, visible text, native progress, bounded live status, and responsive collapse.
risksAndRecovery.rollback: Remove the new progress domain/projection surfaces and restore the prior per-skill scalar/trace implementation; no persisted data migration is required.
risksAndRecovery.forwardRecovery: If the model grows beyond the simulator, freeze the in-memory contract and add a persistence/adapter plan rather than silently introducing backend behavior.
